title: Job interviews
subtitle: shortlisted, trial run, notice period, an ideal fit
summary: Handle the whole interview process in English - being shortlisted, doing your homework, facing a panel, and reading the job offer email.

lesson.heading: Before the interview
lesson.text: When companies are **recruiting** (hiring new staff), they use a set of **criteria** - requirements they use to make a decision, such as three years of experience in the field. If you are **shortlisted**, you have been selected from a larger group, so **do your homework**: find out as much as you can about the company, its products, markets and competitors.

examples.text: We are **recruiting** people for our new branch in the city centre.
Describe your experience to show how you fulfil all the **criteria** for the job.
They just called me to say I have been **shortlisted** for an interview.

lesson.heading: Practice and confidence
lesson.text: If you can, ask a friend to do a **trial run** with you - a practice of something new. This will help **boost** your confidence, that is improve or increase it. The interview may be **conducted by a panel**, a group of people, probably including your future **line manager**, the person directly responsible for your work.

examples.text: Do a **trial run** to practise how you will answer the interview questions.
Smiling will make you seem more friendly, and might actually **boost** your confidence too.
The **panel** of interviewers will include your future **line manager**.

lesson.heading: First impressions
lesson.text: As you arrive, **body language** - physical movements which show how you are feeling - is important. Give a **firm handshake**, **make eye contact** with all the interviewers while you are talking, and **speak up**, that is speak more loudly and clearly. All of this helps to **create a good first impression**.

examples.text: Make sure you greet your interviewer with a **firm handshake**.
Don't forget to **make eye contact** with all the interviewers - look at them directly.
I'm afraid you'll have to **speak up**. I can hardly hear what you're saying.
Dress smartly and professionally to **create a good first impression**.

lesson.heading: Questions and answers in the interview
lesson.text: An interviewer may ask you to **talk them through** your CV - to tell them about it in more detail - or to give an example of how you have **worked well under pressure**. A **trainee** is a person who is learning a new job; **new recruits** are people who have just joined the company.

examples.text: *A:* So, can you **talk us through** your CV?
*B:* Well, I studied Engineering and then took a job as a **trainee** at F3 Telecom.
Can you give us an example of how you've worked **under pressure**?
How would your colleagues or your **supervisor** describe you?
examples.note: supervisor = the person who checks your work

lesson.heading: Development, responsibility and starting
lesson.text: **Professional development** is training given to employees to increase their knowledge or skills; **in-house** training happens within the company. If you are keen to **take on** more responsibility, say so. The company may want to **fill the post** quickly, so they will ask about your **notice period** - the time you must still work after officially telling your employer you are leaving.

examples.text: We have a very good **in-house** training programme for **new recruits**.
If I get the new job, I will have to **take on** more responsibility, but I will get a salary increase.
If we can't **fill** the post internally, we'll have to advertise externally.
The **notice period** on my present job is just two weeks, so I could start very soon.

lesson.heading: The job offer email
lesson.text: A good offer letter says your qualifications and experience will be **an ideal fit for** the job, that is very suitable for it. It attaches a document **outlining** (giving an overview of) your salary, benefits including **paid leave** - time off you are paid for, such as holiday or parental leave - and the **reporting structure**.

examples.text: We are delighted to **offer you the position** of Trainee Programmer.
We believe your qualifications and experience will be **an ideal fit for** the job.
Please review the attached document **outlining** your salary, benefits (including **paid leave**) and **reporting structure**.
Once we have received the paperwork, we will contact you to arrange your **start date**.

lesson.text: Watch the exact forms: it is a supervisor (not a superior), in-house training (not in-office), a notice period (not a leaving period) and a trainee (not a trainer).

exercises.prompt: Before the interview, do your ___: find out as much as you can about the company.
exercises.explanation: To do your homework is to prepare thoroughly before an event.

exercises.prompt: If you can, do a ___ to practise how you will answer the interview questions.
exercises.hint: (two words: a practice of something new)
exercises.explanation: A trial run is a practice of something new.

exercises.prompt: You need to create a good ___ with the interviewers. Dress smartly and professionally.
exercises.explanation: What people think of you at the start is your first impression.

exercises.prompt: Remember that your ___ also plays an important part. Don't forget to smile!
exercises.hint: (two words: physical movements showing how you feel)
exercises.explanation: Body language is the physical movements which show how you are feeling.

exercises.prompt: Smiling might actually ___ your confidence too.
exercises.explanation: To boost something is to improve or increase it.

exercises.prompt: Make sure you greet your interviewer with a ___ handshake.
exercises.explanation: A firm handshake makes a good first impression.

exercises.prompt: Make ___ contact when you talk to them - look at them directly.
exercises.explanation: You make eye contact with the people you are talking to.

exercises.prompt: Describe your education and experience to show how you fulfil all the ___ for the job.
exercises.hint: (plural: requirements used to make a decision)
exercises.explanation: Criteria are the requirements a company uses to choose the most suitable candidates. The singular is criterion.

exercises.prompt: I'm afraid you'll have to ___. I can hardly hear what you're saying.
exercises.explanation: To speak up is to speak more loudly and clearly.

exercises.prompt: If we can't ___ the post internally, we'll have to advertise externally.
exercises.explanation: You fill a post - that is, find someone to do the job.

exercises.prompt: If I get the new job, I will have to take ___ more responsibility.
exercises.explanation: To take on responsibility is to start to have it.

exercises.prompt: I don't like working ___. I end up making mistakes.
exercises.explanation: The fixed collocation is to work under pressure.

exercises.prompt: As part of the programme of ___, we would like to invite you to a session on project management.
exercises.explanation: Professional development is training given to employees to increase their knowledge or skills.

exercises.statement: Please find attached a document overviewing your working conditions.
exercises.explanation: The verb is outline: Please find attached a document outlining your working conditions.

exercises.statement: In some companies the leaving period can be as much as six months.
exercises.explanation: It is called the notice period: In some companies the notice period can be as much as six months.

exercises.statement: The company doesn't do any in-office training. It's all done externally.
exercises.explanation: Training within the company is in-house training: The company doesn't do any in-house training.

exercises.statement: I'm a trainee accountant. I haven't passed my qualifying exams yet.
exercises.explanation: Correct - a trainee is a person who is learning a new job. A trainer teaches other people.

exercises.prompt: Match each word or phrase with its meaning.

pairs.right: selected from a larger group of candidates
the person directly responsible for your work
the person who checks your work
people who have just joined the company
time off you still receive your salary for

exercises.prompt: Does each phrase belong to preparing for the interview or to the job offer?
Put this interview question in order.
exercises.answer: So, can you talk us through your CV?
exercises.explanation: To talk someone through something is to tell them about it in more detail.
